hints.title: What information do you need first?
hints.body: The answer depends on how many times each distinct value occurs, not on where it appears. Build a frequency table before thinking about selection.

hints.title: Turn the table into a ranking
hints.body: Each distinct value becomes a pair `(value, count)`. Sort those pairs by count descending, and for equal counts by value ascending. The first `k` pairs identify the selected values.

hints.title: Do not forget the output order
hints.body: After choosing the top `k`, sort the chosen values numerically before returning them. This is different from the ranking order. Python's `Counter` plus a tuple sort key, or a min-heap of size `k`, both work.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
counts = map from value to occurrence count
pairs = list of (value, count) for every key in counts
sort pairs by (-count, value)
chosen = values of the first k pairs
sort chosen in ascending order
return chosen
```

A heap implementation can replace the full sort. This is pseudocode, not a complete solution.
